title: Putting a number on a founder’s voice
excerpt: INPUT Global published a personal branding framework with an open formula: the Voice Index, a 0–100 score built on median reach and five quality signals. The arithmetic is worth reading. So are its seams.
content_html:
TL;DR

INPUT Global released Voice, a personal branding framework with a published formula. The Voice Index scores founders 0–100 by multiplying logarithmic median reach by a quality multiplier (0.85–1.10) built from five weighted signals. It excludes followers and averages by design. The model has real seams: the January and July versions are structurally incompatible, the agency scores what it sells, and paid placements count toward quality. But publishing the arithmetic at all is unusual for the genre.

Every few months another agency pitches me a personal-branding framework, and the pitches tend to land in the same place, with stages, arrows, and a trademark symbol above advice that circulated a decade ago. Publish more often, get quoted somewhere respectable, trust the algorithm; the genre rarely rewards close reading.

INPUT Global, a communications agency focusing on emerging tech brands, released an expanded version of one such framework in late July, dubbed Voice. It sorts personal brand growth into six stages and, unusually, ends in a number: the Voice Index, a 0–100 score for how far a founder’s words actually travel. The release is unusual in one narrow respect, in that the agency published the arithmetic behind that score. Framework authors rarely expose a formula to readers inclined to check it, which earned this one a few days of my time.

Frameworks that came before this one

Agencies have circled this problem for years.

Golin’s CEO Impact Index, launched in 2024 and updated twice a year since, scores Fortune 250 chief executives on eight visibility criteria; its top fifty averaged 80% higher annual share-price growth than comparable Fortune 250 peers.

Academic work has moved more cautiously, and a 2025 Administrative Sciences paper argued that personal branding still lacks a standardised way to measure brand equity. Both stopped at the boardroom door, leaving founders one tier below outside the sample, which happens to be where most reputation spending occurs.

Voice was introduced in January this year and expanded on the agency’s site in July, dividing personal brand growth into six stages: Origin, Foundational Posting, Distribution, Author’s Format, Authority and Signature Show. INPUT Global’s co-founder Oleg Bevz described the underlying complaint in a March interview, arguing that most founders navigate on likes, conference compliments and instinct.

Inside the arithmetic

Bolted to this ladder sits the Voice Index, which resolves everything into a single figure between 0 and 100, multiplying Reach by Quality. Reach runs on a logarithmic curve calibrated per platform, anchored on whichever channel a founder sounds loudest on, with every additional platform contributing a fifth of its own weight. Each tenfold gain buys a comparable step upward, so 12,500 median views on X score 40 points and 100 arrives only at 350,000.

Two design choices give the model teeth, the first being that median reach replaces averages, since one viral post reports luck more than audience. The agency cites research finding a median of 35 views against a mean of 2,335 on X, with the top 1% of posts absorbing three-quarters of all impressions. Followers are excluded outright as purchasable and uninformative about who sees a post.

Quality then adjusts the result within a band of roughly 0.85 to 1.10, assembled from five weighted signals like Presence at 15%, Distribution at 25%, Resonance at 20%, Authority at 25%, and Signature Show at 15%. Narrowness there is deliberate, since effort can tune loudness without manufacturing it, and the published worked example moves a mid-scale founder only three points when two signals climb from average to strong.

Seams in the model

Three things gave me pause, beginning with the discovery that the July Index differs structurally from the version described in January. That earlier model used five differently weighted components on a 0–1 scale, leaving figures from the two systems impossible to compare.

Questions about who marks the work follow closely, given that INPUT Global designs the Index, computes the score, sells the service meant to raise it, and reports the improvement. No outside party verifies any step. Distribution carries a quarter of the Quality weighting with paid placements counted, which sits awkwardly against the claim that a strong score cannot be bought.

Industry appetite for measurable claims

Andrey Trubetskoy, chief executive and co-founder of the Dubai agency JETA, locates the framework’s value where I do, in measurability. Nearly two decades of work for clients like Dubai Multi Commodities Centre and Visa have shaped his view of what personal branding has lacked, and he reads methods like Voice as pulling agency practice toward data-led standards clients will eventually demand as routine.

Such caveats do not sink the exercise, since a composite score that forces a founder to name their bottleneck beats a feeling, and publishing the bands alongside a documented before-and-after makes disagreement possible. Whether the figure earns wider trust turns on something the agency cannot supply alone, namely somebody outside running the same numbers and arriving in the same place.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

INPUT Global 发布了 Voice，这是一个具有公开公式的个人品牌框架。 Voice Index 通过对数中位数乘以由五个加权信号构建的质量乘数 (0.85-1.10) 为创始人评分 0-100。 它在设计上排除了追随者和平均值。 该模型确实存在缺陷：一月和七月的版本在结构上不兼容，该机构对其销售的产品进行评分，付费展示也计入质量。 但出版算术对于这一类型来说是不寻常的。

每隔几个月，就会有另一家机构向我推销个人品牌框架，而这些推销往往都在同一个地方，在十年前流传的建议之上有舞台、箭头和商标符号。 更频繁地发布、在受人尊敬的地方被引用、信任算法；这种类型很少奖励仔细阅读。

INPUT Global 是一家专注于新兴科技品牌的传播机构，于 7 月底发布了此类框架的扩展版本，名为 Voice。 它将个人品牌成长分为六个阶段，并且不同寻常的是，以一个数字结尾：声音指数，0-100 分，衡量创始人言语的实际传播程度。 这次发布在一个狭隘的方面是不寻常的，因为该机构公布了该分数背后的算术。 框架作者很少向愿意检查它的读者公开公式，这为我赢得了几天的时间。

在此之前的框架

多年来，各机构一直在关注这个问题。

Golin 的首席执行官影响力指数于 2024 年推出，此后每年更新两次，根据八项可见性标准对《财富》250 强首席执行官进行评分；与财富 250 强同行相比，该公司排名前 50 名的股价年增长率平均高出 80%。

学术工作变得更加谨慎，2025 年行政科学论文指出，个人品牌仍然缺乏衡量品牌资产的标准化方法。 两人都停在了董事会门口，将创始人留在样本之外，而这恰好是大多数声誉支出发生的地方。

Voice 于今年 1 月推出，并于 7 月在该机构网站上扩展，将个人品牌成长分为六个阶段：起源、基础发布、分发、作者格式、权威和签名展示。 INPUT Global 的联合创始人奥列格·贝夫兹 (Oleg Bevz) 在 3 月份的一次采访中描述了潜在的抱怨，认为大多数创始人都是靠点赞、会议赞美和本能来导航的。

算术里面

与这个梯子相连的是语音指数，它将所有内容解析为 0 到 100 之间的一个数字，即覆盖率乘以质量。 Reach 运行在每个平台校准的对数曲线上，锚定在创始人声音最大的频道上，每个额外的平台贡献其自身权重的五分之一。 每增加十倍就相当于向上迈了一步，因此 X 评分为 40 分和 100 分的观看次数中位数为 12,500 次，最终只有 350,000 次。

模型牙齿有两种设计选择，第一个是中位覆盖范围取代了平均覆盖范围，因为一篇病毒式传播的帖子报道说运气比观众多。 该机构援引研究发现，X 上的平均浏览量为 35 次，而平均浏览量为 2,335 次，排名前 1% 的帖子占据了所有印象数的四分之三。 追随者被彻底排除在外，因为他们可以购买并且无法提供有关谁看到帖子的信息。

然后，质量会在大约 0.85 到 1.10 的范围内调整结果，该范围由五个加权信号组合而成，例如存在性 15%、分布 25%、共振 20%、权威 25% 和签名显示 15%。 那里的狭窄是故意的，因为努力可以调整响度而不需要制造它，并且当两个信号从平均上升到强时，已发布的工作示例仅使中型创始人移动三分。

模型中的接缝

三件事让我犹豫不决，首先是发现七月指数在结构上与一月描述的版本不同。 早期的模型在 0-1 范围内使用了五个不同权重的组件，使得两个系统的数据无法进行比较。

鉴于 INPUT Global 设计了指数、计算了分数、销售了旨在提高分数的服务并报告了改进情况，因此关于谁对作品进行评分的问题紧随其后。 没有任何外部方验证任何步骤。 付费排名占质量权重的四分之一，这与“高分是买不来”的说法格格不入。

行业对可衡量索赔的需求

迪拜机构 JETA 的首席执行官兼联合创始人 Andrey Trubetskoy 将框架的价值定位在可衡量性上。 为迪拜多种商品中心和 Visa 等客户工作了近二十年，他对个人品牌建设缺乏什么认识，他将 Voice 等方法视为将代理实践推向客户最终要求的以数据为主导的标准。

这些警告并不会破坏这项工作，因为综合评分迫使创始人说出他们的瓶颈，这会打败感觉，并且将乐队与记录的前后结果一起发布可能会导致分歧。 这个数字是否能赢得更广泛的信任取决于该机构无法单独提供的东西，即外部人员运行相同的数字并到达同一个地方。
